description: Eight additional two-file repository tasks for the iteration-027 independent size-sixteen expansion.

tasks.title: Extend shipping manifest costing
tasks.statement: The repository currently costs simple weight records. Extend it to read a non-negative integer N and N lines id|weight|fragile, where weight is a non-negative whole number and fragile is yes or no. Cost is weight times 5 plus 100 when fragile is yes. Put the complete cost rule in the shipping helper and update the entrypoint consistently. Print id:cost=C in input order, then total=T|fragile=F. With N zero, print only the summary.

parley.main.par:
include "shipping.par"

to main:
    let count_input be ask for a number ""
    let count be value of count_input
    repeat count times:
        let line be ask ""
        let parts be line split by "|"
        let id be item 1 of parts
        let weight be item 2 of parts as number
        say id + ":cost=" + (shipping_cost with weight)
parley.shipping.par:
to shipping_cost with weight as number giving number:
    give back weight * 5

python.main.py:
from shipping import shipping_cost

count = int(input())
for _ in range(count):
    item_id, weight = input().split("|")
    print(f"{item_id}:cost={shipping_cost(int(weight))}")
python.shipping.py:
def shipping_cost(weight: int) -> int:
    return weight * 5

tasks.title: Add role-aware account lockout policy
tasks.statement: The repository currently classifies attempt counts with one lock threshold. Extend it to read a non-negative integer N and N lines user|attempts|role, where attempts is a non-negative whole number and role is admin or member. Admin locks at 10 or more attempts; every other role locks at 5 or more. Put the role-aware rule in the lockout helper and update the entrypoint consistently. Print user:locked or user:open in input order, then locked=L,open=O. With N zero, print only the counts.

parley.lockout.par:
to is_locked with attempts as number giving yesno:
    give back attempts is at least 5
parley.main.par:
include "lockout.par"

to main:
    let count_input be ask for a number ""
    let count be value of count_input
    repeat count times:
        let attempts_input be ask for a number ""
        let attempts be value of attempts_input
        if (is_locked with attempts):
            say "locked"
        otherwise:
            say "open"

python.lockout.py:
def is_locked(attempts: int) -> bool:
    return attempts >= 5
python.main.py:
from lockout import is_locked

count = int(input())
for _ in range(count):
    attempts = int(input())
    print("locked" if is_locked(attempts) else "open")

tasks.title: Add configurable sensor bands
tasks.statement: The repository currently classifies readings against a fixed high threshold. Extend it to read signed whole-number low and high thresholds, a non-negative integer N, then N lines sensor|reading. Classify reading below low as low, above high as high, and both boundary values plus the range between them as normal. Put the complete classification in the sensor helper and update the entrypoint consistently. Print sensor:band in input order, then low=L,normal=N,high=H. With no readings, print only the counts.

public_cases.stdout:
a:low
b:normal
c:normal
d:normal
e:high
low=1,normal=3,high=1

parley.main.par:
include "sensor.par"

to main:
    let count_input be ask for a number ""
    let count be value of count_input
    repeat count times:
        let reading_input be ask for a number ""
        let reading be value of reading_input
        say (sensor_band with reading)
parley.sensor.par:
to sensor_band with reading as number giving text:
    if reading is more than 100:
        give back "high"
    give back "normal"

python.main.py:
from sensor import sensor_band

count = int(input())
for _ in range(count):
    print(sensor_band(int(input())))
python.sensor.py:
def sensor_band(reading: int) -> str:
    return "high" if reading > 100 else "normal"

tasks.title: Add normalized first-seen tag deduplication
tasks.statement: The repository currently lowercases and prints every tag. Extend it to read a non-negative integer N and N tag lines. Normalize each tag with the existing helper using lowercase. Print only the first occurrence of each normalized tag, preserving first-seen order. Then print unique=U,duplicates=D. Equality is exact after lowercasing; tags may be empty. Keep normalization in the helper and uniqueness/counting in the entrypoint. With N zero, print only the summary.

public_cases.stdin:
6
Alpha
alpha
BETA
beta
gamma
ALPHA

parley.main.par:
include "tags.par"

to main:
    let count_input be ask for a number ""
    let count be value of count_input
    repeat count times:
        let tag be ask ""
        say (normalize_tag with tag)
parley.tags.par:
to normalize_tag with tag as text giving text:
    give back lowercase of tag

python.main.py:
from tags import normalize_tag

count = int(input())
for _ in range(count):
    print(normalize_tag(input()))
python.tags.py:
def normalize_tag(tag: str) -> str:
    return tag.lower()

tasks.title: Add overtime-aware timesheet payroll
tasks.statement: The repository currently multiplies one hours/rate pair. Extend it to read a non-negative integer N and N lines employee|hours|rate, where hours and rate are non-negative whole numbers. The first 40 hours pay rate per hour; additional hours pay twice the rate. Put the complete pay rule in the payroll helper and update the entrypoint consistently. Print employee:pay=P in input order, then total=T. With N zero, print only total=0.

parley.main.par:
include "payroll.par"

to main:
    let hours_input be ask for a number ""
    let rate_input be ask for a number ""
    let hours be value of hours_input
    let rate be value of rate_input
    say "pay=" + (calculate_pay with hours, rate)
parley.payroll.par:
to calculate_pay with hours as number, rate as number giving number:
    give back hours * rate

python.main.py:
from payroll import calculate_pay

hours = int(input())
rate = int(input())
print(f"pay={calculate_pay(hours, rate)}")
python.payroll.py:
def calculate_pay(hours: int, rate: int) -> int:
    return hours * rate

tasks.title: Add configurable assessment score bands
tasks.statement: The repository currently labels scores against a fixed pass mark. Extend it to read non-negative whole-number pass_mark and excellence_mark, a non-negative integer N, then N lines user|score. Scores at least excellence_mark are excellent; otherwise scores at least pass_mark pass; lower scores retry. Put the ordered classification in the score helper and update the entrypoint consistently. Print user:band in input order, then excellent=E,pass=P,retry=R. With N zero, print only the counts.

public_cases.stdout:
a:retry
b:pass
c:pass
d:excellent
e:excellent
excellent=2,pass=2,retry=1

parley.main.par:
include "scores.par"

to main:
    let count_input be ask for a number ""
    let count be value of count_input
    repeat count times:
        let score_input be ask for a number ""
        let score be value of score_input
        say (score_band with score)
parley.scores.par:
to score_band with score as number giving text:
    if score is at least 50:
        give back "pass"
    give back "retry"

python.main.py:
from scores import score_band

count = int(input())
for _ in range(count):
    print(score_band(int(input())))
python.scores.py:
def score_band(score: int) -> str:
    return "pass" if score >= 50 else "retry"

tasks.title: Add running-capacity delivery batching
tasks.statement: The repository currently checks each unit request independently against capacity. Extend it to read non-negative whole-number capacity, a non-negative integer N, then N lines id|units. Process requests in input order. Accept a request when used plus units is at most capacity, then add units to used; otherwise defer it and leave used unchanged. Put the acceptance rule in the batch helper and update the entrypoint consistently. Print id:accept or id:defer, then used=U,deferred=D. With N zero, print only the summary.

parley.batch.par:
to can_accept with units as number, capacity as number giving yesno:
    give back units is at most capacity
parley.main.par:
include "batch.par"

to main:
    let capacity_input be ask for a number ""
    let count_input be ask for a number ""
    let capacity be value of capacity_input
    let count be value of count_input
    repeat count times:
        let units_input be ask for a number ""
        let units be value of units_input
        if (can_accept with units, capacity):
            say "accept"
        otherwise:
            say "defer"

python.batch.py:
def can_accept(units: int, capacity: int) -> bool:
    return units <= capacity
python.main.py:
from batch import can_accept

capacity = int(input())
count = int(input())
for _ in range(count):
    units = int(input())
    print("accept" if can_accept(units, capacity) else "defer")

tasks.title: Add owner-aware normalized path slugs
tasks.statement: The repository currently replaces spaces with underscores in bare names. Extend it to read a non-negative integer N and N lines owner|name, where owner has no pipe and name may be empty but has no pipe. The helper must lowercase the name and replace every space with a hyphen. Update the entrypoint to parse records. Print owner:slug in input order, then entries=N,characters=C where C sums slug character lengths. With N zero, print only the summary.

parley.main.par:
include "path_rules.par"

to main:
    let count_input be ask for a number ""
    let count be value of count_input
    repeat count times:
        let name be ask ""
        say (sanitize_name with name)
parley.path_rules.par:
to sanitize_name with name as text giving text:
    give back name replacing " " with "_"

python.main.py:
from path_rules import sanitize_name

count = int(input())
for _ in range(count):
    print(sanitize_name(input()))
python.path_rules.py:
def sanitize_name(name: str) -> str:
    return name.replace(" ", "_")
